_purpose: Machine-readable seat topology. Consumed by seat-worktree-gate (write refuse), branch-safety (registered seat branches are live), and generate-combined (state namespaces). Ownership is from recent writes, not from names.

_snapshot.note: Draft snapshot was b3fa27f. Topology landed at 56f0680 on parent e6de1eb. Main moved under this seat to 4fa70bb (property handover amend) before topology finish. otherWorktrees named 2026-08-20 topology finish. 2026-08-21: operator assigned plan-review, icc-portal and smartcity-os to property, and created the SUBSTRATE seat for hauska-mcp-server and hauska-atom-contract. Before this, SEAT-01 having been armed meant those five repos had NO legal write path at all, which is a stronger consequence than the collision risk the planner first described.
evidence: git log P:/Empressa Trading since 2026-08-15 (TW-68 through TW-74)

_empressaTradingOwnership.why: Observed August writes in empressa-trading are the markets enforcement arc (TW-68 deploy gate, TW-70 sixth state, TW-72 capture halt, TW-73 reading-not-rendering, TW-74 protection-present-is-not-checks-required) cutting through apps/cockpit/backend, tools/deploy_gate, and frontend provenance tiles. A path split is not clean on that evidence. Last-writer-wins is rejected as the ownership rule: it describes who wrote, not who may write next. Product identity (repo_intents: Empressa Cockpit) still names a trading venture. That is why trading remains a registered seat with no exclusive product repo: it requests cockpit changes from markets. Reversal: if trading is seated and writing cockpit product code while markets is still writing spine/gates, declare a path split then (frontend + product routers to trading; spine, capture, deploy_gate to markets) rather than transferring the whole repo.
_empressaTradingOwnership.rejected: path-split by apps/cockpit/frontend vs backend/spine. TW-66 already crossed that boundary in one commit.

integration.name: integration
integration.role: doc_repo primary checkout and merge target. Not a planner seat. Exists so the shared index is a named worktree rather than an unowned default. Planner seats do not do seat work here. The seat-worktree-gate allows this path only on branch main, and refuses writes into another seat's _state namespace from here.

repos.name: smartcity-os
repos.noTouchReason: ABSOLUTE NO-TOUCH standing ruling (repo_intents 2026-07-04): live Bastrop production, pre-spine, fully siloed. Ownership is recorded so the repo is not UNASSIGNED, and NO worktree is registered, so SEAT-01 refuses every write to it. Ownership answers who may lift the ruling; it does not grant a write path. Lifting it means registering a worktree in the same commit that records the operator ruling.

seats.authority: Property substrate and Empressa property/govtech surfaces (incl. plan-review and icc-portal as OPS-17 lane siblings; smartcity-os owned but NO-TOUCH): factory and acquisition (legacy-design-tools), hauska-engine, hauska-map, smartcity-dashboards, smart-files. Writes its own _state/property and _inbox/property-* files. May merge its own branches. Does not write smart-markets or empressa-trading. Does not adjudicate another seat's closed finding.

seats.name: markets
seats.authority: Markets substrate: smart-markets (instrument twin) and empressa-trading (cockpit spine, capture, deploy gate). Writes its own _state/markets files. May merge its own branches. Trading seat requests cockpit product/UX changes from this seat. Does not write property-owned repos.

seats.name: trading
seats.authority: Trading product intent and cockpit UX requests. No exclusive product repository until a path split is declared. Writes its own _state/trading files. Requests empressa-trading changes from markets. Does not write product repos.

seats.name: systems
seats.authority: doc_repo hygiene, enforcement controls, seat topology, branch protection settings, C-00 and sibling gates. Shared canon owner for ENFORCEMENT.md and seat_register.json. Read-only scans of product repos. Does not write product repos. May merge its own branch.

seats.authority: Hauska commercial substrate: the MCP gate and the atom contract. Operator ruling 2026-08-21. Held separate from property because these are substrate, not product surfaces, and because property already carries seven repos. The atom contract is the only artifact in this estate that refuses to compile, which makes it the most authoritative thing here; the MCP server is the single enforcement chokepoint. Writes its own _state/substrate files. May merge its own branches. Does not write property or markets repos. Historical note: cc-agent-M served this scope and had no doc_repo access.

seats.name: govtech
seats.authority: OPS-17 govtech product line: SmartCity Dashboards, plan review, Smart Files and the ICC portal. Created 2026-08-24 on the operator ruling "seat on govtech, i have a long ways to go on the property seat". These four repos moved OFF the property seat, which keeps legacy-design-tools, hauska-engine, hauska-map and smartcity-os. smartcity-os deliberately stays with property and remains ABSOLUTE NO-TOUCH: it is this seat's SUBJECT, not its property, and the v2 replacement is built alongside it and cut over later by a named card. NO BRANCH IS PINNED ON THE PRODUCT REPO ENTRIES, by design: this seat ships through per-PR feature branches, and seat-worktree-gate only enforces a branch when the entry declares one. The doc_repo entry above DOES pin seat/govtech. Writes its own _state/govtech files. May merge its own branches. Does not write property, markets or substrate repos; requests changes there from the owning seat. First work: plan-review PR #6 (Smart Files scope gate + first CI).
